mainTopic: Minimum amounts for liability when carrying out hair, clay, lime, earth, manure, sand, and reeds on שבת
overview: This amud goes through the minimum amounts (שיעורים) that make a person liable for carrying things out on שבת. First a ברייתא gives the amounts for hair and clay. Then the גמרא explains the משנה's amount for lime, which leads to a side discussion about smearing girls with lime, the meaning of שמן המור, and the story of רב ביבי. Next the גמרא tries to define the words כלכול and אנדיפי in the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה. רב's explanation is rejected because of רבי's statement about dissolved lime versus lumps. The גמרא then tries several other explanations: lime on wine vessels, measuring marks (רב כהנא), and the forehead. A new משנה follows, giving the amounts for earth, manure, sand, and reeds. The גמרא explains the plasterer's trowel and asks whose view holds that sand improves plaster. It leaves רב אשי's question about the reed-pen as תיקו. Finally, it identifies the 'easy egg' as a chicken egg and sets the measure at a גרוגרת's worth of it.

steps.title: Amounts for carrying hair and clay
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the minimum amounts of hair and clay for liability when carrying them out on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who carries out hair is liable for enough to knead clay with it. For clay, the amount is enough to make the opening of a goldsmiths' furnace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds two more items to the משנה's list of minimum amounts. These are hair and clay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule on שבת is that you are only liable for carrying something if it is a useful amount. Hair was mixed into clay to make it stronger. So the amount for hair is what is needed for that job. The amount for clay is what a goldsmith needs to shape the opening where the bellows go into the furnace.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries out (from one domain to another on שבת)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who carries out hair
is liable for enough to knead clay with it.
phrases.notes: Hair was mixed into clay to strengthen it.

phrases.english: Clay: enough to make the opening of a furnace
of gold refiners.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hair: enough to knead into clay. Clay: enough to form the bellows opening of a goldsmith's furnace.

steps.title: Defining the amount for lime
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's amount for lime, and a תנא makes it more precise: enough for the finger of the smallest girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: lime, enough to smear. A תנא taught: enough to smear the little finger of the smallest of girls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about lime. Then it brings a ברייתא that makes the amount more exact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'enough to smear on the smallest girl.' The ברייתא adds that this means just her little finger, which is a very small amount. This sets up the next step, which explains why girls were smeared with lime in the first place.

phrases.english: Lime: enough to smear.
A Tanna taught: enough to smear
the little finger of the smallest of girls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא's items to the משנה's next item, lime.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lime amount is enough to smear the little finger of the smallest girl.

steps.title: How girls were prepared: lime, flour, or myrrh oil
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that girls who matured physically before their age were smeared to remove hair. Each social class used a different substance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Jewish girls who matured physically before reaching the age of maturity were smeared. Poor girls were smeared with lime. Rich girls were smeared with fine flour. Princesses were smeared with myrrh oil, as the verse says: 'Six months with myrrh oil.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains why girls were smeared with lime. This is background for the משנה's measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Girls who developed body hair before the usual age had it removed. Poor families used lime, which is cheap and harsh. Rich families used fine flour, and royalty used שמן המור. The verse from מגילת אסתר proves that royalty used שמן המור.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Jewish girls who reached physical maturity
but had not yet reached the age of maturity,
daughters of the poor were smeared with lime.
Daughters of the wealthy were smeared with fine flour,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹת מְלָכִים — טוֹפְלוֹת אוֹתָן בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמּוֹר,
phrases.english: daughters of kings were smeared with myrrh oil,
as it says: 'Six months with myrrh oil.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the background behind smearing girls with lime.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Early-maturing girls were smeared for hair removal: the poor with lime, the rich with flour, and royalty with שמן המור.

steps.title: What is myrrh oil?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly שמן המור is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is myrrh oil?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the term שמן המור, which came up in the verse. This sets up two answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase comes from a verse, but the actual substance is not obvious. The גמרא wants a clear identification.

phrases.english: What is myrrh oil?

steps.title: Two identifications of myrrh oil
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא says it is סטכת (oil of myrrh). רב ירמיה בר אבא says it is oil from olives less than a third grown.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said: It is סטכת. רב ירמיה בר אבא said: It is olive oil from olives that have not reached a third of their growth.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers to the question of what שמן המור is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר חייא identifies it as a known perfume called סטכת. רב ירמיה בר אבא says it is oil from very unripe olives. That oil is sharp and acidic, which makes it work for removing hair.

keyTerms.meaning: סטכת, a type of myrrh perfume oil
That has not reached a third of its growth

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר: סְטָכַת.
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chiya said: Setaket.
Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
Olive oil from olives that have not reached a third of their growth.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either סטכת, or oil from olives less than a third ripe.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting the unripe olive oil view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה describes אנפיקנון as oil from unripe olives, used to remove hair and soften skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says: אנפיקנון is olive oil from olives that have not reached a third of their growth. Why is it smeared on? Because it removes hair and softens the skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב ירמיה בר אבא's description and explains why this oil was used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms that oil from unripe olives was a known substance with a name, אנפיקנון. It also explains its two effects: it removes hair and softens skin. This fits well with using it to prepare girls.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אַנְפִּיקְנוּן — שֶׁמֶן זַיִת שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא שְׁלִישׁ.
phrases.english: Anfiknon is olive oil from olives that have not reached a third of their growth.
And why is it smeared on?
Because it removes the hair and softens the skin.

steps.raayaObject: רב ירמיה בר אבא's identification of שמן המור as oil from unripe olives.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה about אנפיקנון.

steps.title: The story of רב ביבי's daughter and the neighbor
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי carefully smeared his daughter with lime, one limb at a time, and married her off well. A gentile neighbor smeared his daughter all at once, and she died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי had a daughter. He smeared her with lime limb by limb, and he received four hundred זוזים for her. There was a gentile in his neighborhood who had a daughter. He smeared her all at once, and she died. He said: רב ביבי killed my daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows how lime smearing was done, and how dangerous it is when done wrongly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ביבי applied the lime slowly, one part of the body at a time. His daughter became beautiful and received a large sum at her marriage. The neighbor copied him but used the harsh lime on her whole body at once, which killed her. He blamed רב ביבי.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai had a daughter.
He smeared her limb by limb,
and he received four hundred zuz for her.
There was a certain gentile in his neighborhood.
He had a daughter.
He smeared her all at once, and she died.
He said: Rav Beivai killed my daughter.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lime smearing must be done gradually. Doing it all at once can be deadly.

steps.title: רב נחמן: only beer drinkers need this
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן comments that רב ביבי's family drank beer, which causes hair growth, so they needed smearing. Those who do not drink beer do not need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: רב ביבי, who drinks beer, his daughters need smearing. We, who do not drink beer, our daughters do not need smearing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן ends the story with a comment that limits the need for this practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drinking beer was thought to cause extra body hair. So the practice was only needed in beer-drinking places like רב ביבי's. Where people did not drink beer, there was no need for it.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Rav Beivai, who drinks beer,
his daughters need smearing.
We, who do not drink beer,
our daughters do not need smearing.

steps.whatToRemember: The lime smearing practice explains the משנה's measure. רב נחמן limits the need for it to places where people drink beer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Smearing was only necessary for those whose diet (beer) caused hair growth.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יהודה's measure for lime
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, where רבי יהודה says the lime amount is enough to smear a כלכול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: enough to smear a כלכול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה to set up a discussion of its unclear terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה gives the measure as enough for a כלכול, and רבי נחמיה says enough for an אנדיפי. Both words are unclear, so the גמרא will ask what they mean.

keyTerms.meaning: כלכול, an unclear term (an area of the head or temple)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
enough to smear a kilkul.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר כְּדֵי לָסוּד כִּלְכּוּל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the lime measure is enough to smear a כלכול.

steps.title: What are כלכול and אנדיפי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the two terms used by רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is כלכול, and what is אנדיפי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the two unclear words in the משנה's dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without knowing what these words mean, we cannot know the size of each measure.

keyTerms.meaning: אנדיפי, רבי נחמיה's term in the משנה

phrases.english: What is kilkul, and what is andifi?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definitions of כלכול and אנדיפי.

steps.title: רב: the temple and the area below it
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that both terms refer to areas of the face: the temple and the area beneath the temple.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The temple and the area beneath the temple.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the two terms are two neighboring spots on the side of the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, כלכול is the temple, and אנדיפי is the area just below it. Lime was smeared on these spots to remove or flatten small hairs.

phrases.english: Rav said: The temple and the area beneath the temple.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כלכול is the temple, and אנדיפי is the area beneath the temple.

steps.title: Is רבי יהודה's measure really the larger one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's explanation, because it seems to make רבי יהודה's measure larger, against an established rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבי יהודה's measure is larger? But we hold that the רבנן's measure is larger!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's explanation based on a known pattern about whose measure is bigger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If כלכול is the larger temple area, then רבי יהודה's measure would be large. But there is an accepted rule that the first, anonymous view (the רבנן) has the larger measure in this משנה. The question is how רב's reading fits with that rule.

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Yehuda's measure is larger?
But we have established
that the Rabbis' measure is larger!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's reading seems to make רבי יהודה's measure the largest, which goes against the rule that the רבנן's measure is largest.

steps.title: In the middle: smaller than the רבנן, larger than רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה's measure is smaller than the רבנן's but larger than רבי נחמיה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is smaller than the רבנן's measure and larger than רבי נחמיה's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by placing רבי יהודה's measure in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's reading only makes רבי יהודה's measure larger than רבי נחמיה's. It is still smaller than the רבנן's. So the rule that the רבנן's measure is largest still holds.

phrases.english: It is smaller than the Rabbis' measure,
and larger than Rabbi Nechemya's.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's reading makes רבי יהודה's measure the largest of all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order is: רבנן largest, רבי יהודה in the middle, רבי נחמיה smallest.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי: dissolved lime versus lumps
steps.stepSummary: רבי says רבי יהודה's measure fits dissolved lime and רבי נחמיה's fits lumps of lime. That does not work if both terms are spots on the face.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבי said: רבי יהודה's words seem right for dissolved lime, and רבי נחמיה's words for a lump of lime. If you think the terms mean the temple and the area below it, then both would be dissolved lime!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's definitions using a ברייתא in which רבי ties each opinion to a different form of lime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי says the two opinions deal with two different kinds of lime: wet paste and solid lumps. But if both terms are spots on the face, both would use the same wet paste, since you smear paste on skin. So רב's explanation cannot be correct.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rebbi said:
Rabbi Yehuda's words seem right for dissolved lime,
and Rabbi Nechemya's words for a lump of lime.
And if you would think
that they mean the temple and the area beneath the temple,
then both this and that would be dissolved lime!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's definition of כלכול and אנדיפי as the temple and the area beneath it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי separates the opinions into paste versus lumps. But two spots on the face would both use paste, so there would be no difference between them.
steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not about the size of the measures. It is about the form of the lime (paste versus lump), which shows the two terms cannot both be body parts.

steps.title: New explanation: אנדיפי means the wine jug
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי אמי explains that רבי נחמיה's אנדיפי refers to lime used on wine vessels, not to a spot on the face.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יצחק said that the school of רבי אמי said: It refers to the אנדיפא, the wine vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב's explanation and gives a new meaning for רבי נחמיה's term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the earlier explanation is being replaced. אנדיפי refers to lime applied to wine vessels, and lumps of lime were used for that. Now רבי's distinction works: רבי יהודה deals with paste on the body, and רבי נחמיה deals with lumps used on vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: They said in the study hall of

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yitzchak said:
they said in the study hall of Rabbi Ami:
It refers to the andifa (the lime on wine vessels).
phrases.notes: Lime was applied to earthenware wine vessels.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of a term (replaces רב's explanation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both terms are spots on the face, so both would use dissolved lime.
steps.terutzMaskana: אנדיפי is lime for wine vessels, which uses lumps of lime. This fits רבי's distinction.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's 'temple and the area below it' reading falls away. דבי רבי אמי say רבי נחמיה's אנדיפי is lime used on wine vessels (lumps), while רבי יהודה's כלכול uses dissolved lime. רב כהנא challenges this right away in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a ruling about the physical form of a substance (paste or lump) can decide the meaning of a disputed word in the משנה.

steps.title: רב כהנא objects to wasting lime on wine vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא challenges the school of רבי אמי. Nobody would smear lime inside a wine vessel and ruin both the lime and the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא objected: Would a person turn his money into a loss?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא attacks the answer from Step 15, which said רבי נחמיה's אנדיפי means lime put on wine vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If lime were smeared inside a wine barrel, it would spoil the wine and waste the lime. People do not normally do something that destroys their own property. So this cannot be the normal use that the משנה's measure for lime is based on.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana strongly objected to it:
And does a person turn his money into a loss?!
phrases.notes: Both the lime and the wine would be ruined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that אנדיפי is lime smeared on wine vessels.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People do not destroy their own goods, and smearing lime inside a wine vessel ruins both the lime and the wine.

steps.title: The lime is used for measuring marks on the outside of a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that the lime is used to draw measuring lines on a vessel, like the marks on the הין in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב כהנא said: It means markings. As we learned: There were markings on the הין: up to here for a bull, up to here for a ram, up to here for a sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives his own explanation. The lime is used to mark lines on a vessel, not to coat its inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lime used as an outside marker does not ruin anything. He brings proof that measuring lines existed: the הין vessel in the מקדש had marks showing how much wine to pour for each kind of קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid-measuring vessel used in the מקדש
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Kahana said: Markings.
As we learned: There were markings on the hin —
up to here for a bull,
up to here for a ram,
up to here for a sheep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that Step 16 rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of the use of the lime
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lime was smeared inside the wine vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lime marks measuring lines on the outside of the vessel, which wastes nothing.

steps.title: A second answer: אנדיפא means the forehead
steps.stepSummary: Another answer says אנדיפא is the forehead. Thick lime is smeared there to soften the skin, not to remove hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: What is אנדיפא? The forehead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, separate answer to the question from Step 14 about רבי נחמיה's measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אנדיפא is still a place on the face, the forehead. But lime is put there for a different purpose (softening the skin), so thick lumps of lime work. That fits רבי's statement that רבי נחמיה's measure matches lumpy lime.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)
A body area here explained as the forehead

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
What is "andifa"? The forehead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to Step 14, alongside רב כהנא's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If אנדיפא is a spot on the face, thick lime would not fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is the forehead, where thick lime is smeared to soften the skin.

steps.title: A story proves that אנדיפי means forehead
steps.stepSummary: A Galilean in בבל offered to teach מעשה מרכבה. A hornet stung him on his אנדיפי and he died, and the word clearly means forehead there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like that Galilean who came to בבל. They said to him: Stand and teach us מעשה מרכבה. He said to them: I will teach you as רבי נחמיה taught his colleague. A hornet came out of the wall, stung him on his forehead, and he died. They said about him: From his own, this came to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story where the word אנדיפי is used, to show that it means forehead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story the hornet stung the man on his אנדיפי, so the word is used for the forehead. The closing line means he brought the punishment on himself by trying to teach the secret מעשה מרכבה in public.

keyTerms.meaning: The deep secret teachings about the Divine Chariot, not taught in public
From his own, this came to him (he caused his own punishment)

phrases.english: And like that certain Galilean
who happened to come to Babylonia,
to whom they said: Stand and teach us
the "Act of the Divine Chariot."
He said to them: I will teach you
as Rabbi Nechemya taught his colleague.
And a hornet came out of the wall
and stung him on his forehead, and he died.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מִן דִּילֵיהּ דָּא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: And they said about him: From his own, this came to him.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: he was punished because of his own arrogance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the definition given in Step 18.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the Galilean stung on his אנדיפי by a hornet.
steps.whatToRemember: The lime discussion ends with two answers for רבי נחמיה's measure: measuring lines on a vessel (רב כהנא), or smearing the forehead.

steps.title: New משנה: the measure for carrying earth
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the measure for earth is enough to seal a large sack. חכמים say it is enough to seal a letter.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Earth — enough for the seal of large sacks, the words of רבי עקיבא. And חכמים say: Enough for the seal of letters.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the minimum amounts of different materials that make a person liable for carrying them on שבת, starting with earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earth was used to seal containers so that tampering would show. רבי עקיבא sets the measure by a big sack's seal. חכמים set a much smaller measure, the seal on a letter.

phrases.english: Mishna:
Earth — equal to the seal of large sacks,
the words of Rabbi Akiva.
And the Sages say: equal to the seal of letters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה in the list of carrying measures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earth: רבי עקיבא says the seal of a sack, חכמים say the seal of a letter.

steps.title: The measure for manure and fine sand
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says enough to fertilize one cabbage stalk. חכמים say enough to fertilize a leek.
steps.simpleTranslation: Manure and fine sand — enough to fertilize a stalk of cabbage, the words of רבי עקיבא. And חכמים say: Enough to fertilize a leek.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the measure for manure and fine sand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both materials are used to fertilize plants, so the measure is based on that use. Again חכמים give a smaller amount, since a leek needs less than a cabbage.

phrases.english: Manure and fine sand —
enough to fertilize a stalk of cabbage,
the words of Rabbi Akiva.
And the Sages say: enough to fertilize a leek.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Manure and fine sand: a cabbage stalk's worth (רבי עקיבא) or a leek's worth (חכמים).

steps.title: The measures for coarse sand and a reed
steps.stepSummary: Coarse sand: enough to put on a spoonful of plaster. A reed: enough to make a pen. A thick or broken reed: enough fuel to cook an easy egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: Coarse sand — enough to put on a full spoon of plaster. A reed — enough to make a quill. And if it was thick or broken — enough to cook with it the easiest of eggs, beaten and placed in a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with coarse sand and reeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each measure follows the item's normal use. Coarse sand is mixed into plaster, and a good reed becomes a pen. A reed that cannot be used for writing is only firewood, so its measure is the small amount of fuel needed to cook a beaten egg.

keyTerms.meaning: A pen made from a reed

phrases.aramaic: חוֹל הַגַּס — כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן עַל מְלֹא כַּף סִיד.
phrases.english: Coarse sand — enough to put on a full spoon of plaster.
A reed — enough to make a quill.
And if it was thick or broken —

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לְבַשֵּׁל בּוֹ בֵּיצָה קַלָּה שֶׁבַּבֵּיצִים,
phrases.english: enough to cook with it the easiest of eggs,
beaten and placed in a pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹל הַגַּס כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן עַל מְלֹא כַּף סִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coarse sand: a plaster spoonful. Reed: a pen. Thick or broken reed: fuel to cook a beaten egg.

steps.title: The spoon is a plasterer's trowel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא clarifies that the משנה's כף means the plasterer's trowel, not an eating spoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: "On a full spoon of plaster." It was taught: Enough to put on the mouth of the plasterers' trowel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and explains which spoon the משנה means in the coarse-sand measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כף could mean an ordinary spoon. The ברייתא says it is the tool a plasterer uses, which tells us the size of the measure.

phrases.english: Gemara:
"On a full spoon of plaster."

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן עַל פִּי כַּף שֶׁל סַיָּידִין.
phrases.english: It was taught: enough to put on the mouth of the plasterers' trowel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a phrase from Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measure is the amount placed on a plasterer's trowel.

steps.title: Which תנא holds that sand is good for plaster?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows, since it assumes sand is mixed into plaster.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that sand is good for plaster?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא believes sand improves plaster, because the משנה treats mixing them as a normal use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measure for sand only makes sense if people normally mix sand into plaster. The גמרא wants to know who holds that view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (which opinion is this)?

phrases.aramaic: מַאן תְּנָא דְּחוֹל מְעַלֵּי לֵיהּ לְסִיד?
phrases.english: Who is the tanna who holds that sand is good for plaster?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source opinion behind the משנה's sand measure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that sand is a helpful additive to plaster.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it is רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids sand in mourning-plaster because sand makes good white cement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי יהודה. As it was taught: A person may not plaster his house with plaster unless he mixed straw or sand into it. רבי יהודה says: Straw is permitted, sand is forbidden, because it makes cement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the משנה is רבי יהודה, and he proves it from a ברייתא about plastering houses after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To mourn the חורבן, plain white plaster is not allowed, so something must be mixed in to spoil it. רבי יהודה forbids sand because sand actually makes strong white cement. This shows he holds that sand improves plaster, just like the משנה assumes.
steps.confusionAlert: The ruling is about mourning for the בית המקדש, not about שבת. The גמרא uses it only to find out who holds that sand makes plaster better.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: לֹא יָסוּד אָדָם אֶת בֵּיתוֹ בְּסִיד,
phrases.english: as it was taught: A person may not plaster his house with plaster,
phrases.notes: In mourning for the חורבן of the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עֵירַב בּוֹ תֶּבֶן אוֹ חוֹל.
phrases.english: unless he mixed straw or sand into it.
Rabbi Yehuda says: Straw is permitted,
sand is forbidden, because it makes cement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds that sand turns plaster into strong cement.

steps.title: רבא: it can follow the רבנן too
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה can follow the רבנן as well. For them sand spoils plaster, but after the חורבן that spoiling is exactly what is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even if you say it is the רבנן — its ruining is its fixing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the question of Step 24. The משנה does not have to follow only רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that sand weakens plaster. But since one may only plaster with spoiled plaster after the חורבן, adding sand makes the plaster usable. Either way, sand has a real use with plaster.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say it follows the רבנן

phrases.english: Rava said: Even if you say it is the Rabbis —
its ruining is its fixing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, so the משנה is not limited to רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even according to the רבנן, sand is useful with plaster, because the spoiled plaster is what is permitted after the חורבן.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא says the משנה is רבי יהודה (sand improves plaster). רבא says it fits everyone (sand spoils plaster, and spoiled plaster is what is needed).

steps.title: How long the reed-pen must be
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the pen in the משנה is one long enough to reach the joints of the fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: "A reed — enough to make a quill." It was taught: A quill that reaches the joints of one's fingers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the reed measure in the משנה and quotes a ברייתא that gives the pen's size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not say how big a pen is. The ברייתא answers: long enough to reach the finger joints when held.

phrases.english: "A reed — enough to make a quill."
It was taught: A quill that reaches the joints of one's fingers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the next item of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pen must be long enough to reach the finger joints.

steps.title: רב אשי asks: which finger joint?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether the ברייתא means the upper joint or the lower joint of the fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: The upper joint or the lower joint?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי raises a question about the ברייתא's measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each finger has more than one joint, so the length is unclear. The answer decides whether the pen measure is shorter or longer.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi raised a question:
The upper joint or the lower joint?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for more detail about the ברייתא in Step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which finger joint sets the pen's minimum length.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question stands (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without answering רב אשי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source settles the matter. The exact pen measure is left in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand (the question is left unresolved)

steps.whatToRemember: The reed measure is a pen reaching the finger joints, but which joint is never decided (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes Step 28's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether the pen must reach the upper or the lower finger joint stays unresolved.

steps.title: The beaten egg is beaten in oil and placed in a pot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a thick reed. A ברייתא adds that the 'beaten' egg is beaten in oil and placed in a stew pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if the reed was thick...' A תנא taught: the egg is beaten in oil and placed in a stew pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about a thick reed used as fuel. A ברייתא explains how the egg in the measure is prepared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thick reed is useless for writing, so it counts only as fuel. Its measure is the fuel needed to cook an egg. The ברייתא says the egg is beaten in oil and set in a pot, which makes it cook quickly. So the amount of fuel needed is small.

keyTerms.meaning: Thick (a reed too thick to write with)

phrases.english: 'And if it was thick, etc.'
It was taught:
Beaten in oil
and placed in a stew pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the pen-length question (תיקו) to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measure for a thick reed is the fuel needed to cook an egg beaten in oil and placed in a stew pot.

steps.title: A father asks his son what an easy egg is
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא asks his son what the משנה means by an 'easy egg'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר, son of רבינא, said to his son: Have you heard what an 'easy egg' is?
steps.whatsHappening: A father tests his son on the meaning of the משנה's term ביצה קלה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of 'an easy egg' but never says which kind. Eggs of different birds cook at different speeds, so the measure depends on which egg is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'easy' egg, one that cooks quickly
Have you heard? (do you know a tradition?)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא לִבְרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, said to his son:
Have you heard
what an easy egg is?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ בֵּיצָה קַלָּה מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which egg the משנה's measure refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of egg is the 'easy egg' of the משנה.

steps.title: The son answers: a turtledove egg
steps.stepSummary: The son says the easy egg is the egg of a turtledove.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The egg of a turtledove.
steps.whatsHappening: The son gives his answer: a turtledove's egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son seems to think 'easy' means small. A small egg would need less fuel to cook.

keyTerms.meaning: The egg of a turtledove (a small bird)

phrases.english: He said to him:
The egg of a turtledove.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the father's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The easy egg is a turtledove egg.

steps.title: If smallness is the reason, a sparrow egg is smaller
steps.stepSummary: The father challenges the answer. If the reason is that the egg is small, then say a sparrow egg, which is even smaller. The son is silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because it is small? Then say the egg of a sparrow! He was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The father attacks the son's answer, and the son has nothing to say back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'easy' just means small, the smallest egg should be the measure, and a sparrow egg is smaller than a turtledove egg. The son cannot defend his choice, so his answer is dropped.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because it is small?
Then say the egg of a sparrow!
He was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא — מִשּׁוּם דְּזוּטְרָא? אֵימָא: דְּצִיפַּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the turtledove answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The son's claim that the easy egg is a turtledove egg.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If size is the reason, an even smaller egg, a sparrow's, should be the measure.
steps.confusionAlert: The silence (אישתיק) is not a new opinion. It just means the son could not defend his answer, so it falls away.

steps.title: Do you know a tradition about this?
steps.stepSummary: After the failed answer, one asks the other whether he has heard any teaching on this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Have you heard anything about this?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the guess failed, they look for a received tradition. This sets up רב ששת's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion moves from reasoning to a known teaching from an earlier Sage.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Have you heard anything about this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a tradition after the son's answer failed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A received teaching that identifies the easy egg.

steps.title: רב ששת: it is a chicken egg
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רב ששת, the answer is that the easy egg is a chicken egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב ששת said this: a chicken egg.
steps.whatsHappening: A tradition from רב ששת settles which egg is meant: a chicken egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This replaces the turtledove answer. 'Easy' does not mean the smallest egg, since a chicken egg is not small.

phrases.english: [He said to him: So]
Rav Sheshet said:
The egg of a chicken.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: בֵּיצַת תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a tradition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The easy egg is a chicken egg.

steps.title: Why a chicken egg is called easy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the name: the חכמים found that no egg cooks more easily than a chicken egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they call it an 'easy egg'? חכמים estimated that no egg is easier to cook than a chicken egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a chicken egg is called 'easy'. 'Easy' means quick to cook, not small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows why the father's challenge was right to reject size as the reason. The measure depends on cooking speed, and the חכמים found the chicken egg cooks fastest. So it needs the least fuel.

phrases.english: And why do they call it an 'easy egg'?
The Sages estimated:
there is no egg as easy to cook
as the egg of a chicken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב ששת's identification.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Easy' means quickest to cook, and the chicken egg cooks quickest.

steps.title: Why an egg here when שבת measures are a dried fig?
steps.stepSummary: The son asks why this measure is an egg, when the measure for food on שבת is usually a גרוגרת (dried fig).
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different? All the measures of שבת are a dried fig, and here it is an egg?
steps.whatsHappening: The son raises a difficulty: the egg measure seems to clash with the standard שבת measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For carrying food on שבת, the usual amount is the size of a dried fig. An egg is bigger than that. So why does the משנה use a full egg here?

keyTerms.meaning: A dried fig, the standard שבת measure for food
The measures of liability on שבת

phrases.english: And what is different
that all measures of Shabbat are a dried fig,
and here it is like an egg?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא כׇּל שִׁיעוּרֵי שַׁבָּת כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת וְהָכָא כְּבֵיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the egg measure itself against the general שבת rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's use of an egg as the measure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבת measures are normally a dried fig, which is smaller than an egg. So the egg measure seems out of line.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a dried fig's worth of the easy egg
steps.stepSummary: The father quotes רב נחמן: the measure is the fuel to cook a dried fig's amount of the easy egg, not the whole egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב נחמן said this: a dried fig's amount from an easy egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The father answers with רב נחמן's teaching. The measure is really a גרוגרת, the size of a dried fig, taken from the egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The egg measure does not break the usual שבת rule. One is liable for carrying enough fuel to cook a dried fig's amount of the quick-cooking egg. So the standard גרוגרת measure stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: A dried fig's amount out of the egg

steps.whatToRemember: The 'easy egg' is a chicken egg, because it cooks the fastest. Carrying a thick reed makes one liable for enough fuel to cook a dried fig's amount of that egg, so the usual שבת measure of גרוגרת is kept.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's unusual-sounding measure still follows the standard שבת measure of a dried fig.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Rav Nachman said this:
A dried fig's amount from an easy egg.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת מִבֵּיצָה קַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash between the egg measure and the dried-fig measure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The measure is the fuel to cook a whole egg, which would be larger than the usual שבת measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The measure is the fuel to cook a dried fig's amount of the egg, which matches the usual שבת measure.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Liability for a thick reed is enough fuel to cook a dried fig's amount of a beaten chicken egg.
